title: Eddie Atkins, Zue Robertson and Roy Palmer
summary: Ridgley recalls Atkins with Joe Oliver, Zue Robertson taught by Batiste, and Roy Palmer in the Tuxedo brass band.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Remember Eddie Atkins? Yeah, he was a good trombone player. Who did they work with?
Eddie Atkins worked with Joe Oliver for a long time. Down here? Yeah. They had a good band. He's there too, huh?
Yes, he is. I've been to his grave. They buried out in Amor, up near Wagamon.

Somewhere. Eddie was a good trombone player. He's buried in the same graveyard as Joe Avery. At that time him and Nora and this other boy, he died, or he must have died with. Now he was a good trombone, Zoo. Zoo? Yeah. Zoo Robertson? Yeah. He was a good trombone player. Who did he work with? He was a Batalier's nephew. Batalier taught him trombone in the beginning. He worked in bands, right, but he played in those cyclic bands until he was a weird familiar up at the time like that. He didn't stay on my own. He was good. He was good. That's right. What about Roy Palmer? Who did he play with? He used to play, him and I, in Tuxedo band together, Palmer trombone. He left here a long time too. In the brass band? Yeah, in the brass band. Did he play dance work too? Oh yeah. He played dance work, but he never was lucky enough to get in a good band now, because that's why he left. But he's a pretty good player.
